reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all 4 files including the PKGBUILD and found standard, safe packaging: GitHub source with pinned SHA256 checksum, standard Python build tools (python -m build, python -m installer), no suspicious commands (curl/wget/eval/base64), no post-install hooks, and operations confined to $srcdir/$pkgdir. Report 1's inconclusive result was due to an API error (HTTP 400), not a security finding, and its initial PKGBUILD audit also found it safe. Report 3 (openrouter/free) failed to parse the model's response format. Only Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) completed successfully and found the package safe. coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b): PKGBUILD review failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError - incomplete coverage
Report 3 (openrouter/free): Failed to parse model response, only reviewed 1 of 4 files, and audited older package version (2.0.0)
learnings: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient API errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent inconclusive results from tool failures
Add response format validation before marking files as reviewed - Report 3's model returned 'User Safety: safe' instead of the expected XML structure
Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine uncertainty' in verdict reporting to avoid false escalation
Ensure version consistency in audit triggers - Report 3 audited pkgver 2.0.0 while current is 2.2.0
